rules.title: Printed status is read before an interface moves
rules.statement: Before a hole, a pocket, a seat or a mating face of a part or of its mate is moved, the print ledger is read: is a copy printed, and from which geometry. An unknown status counts as printed.
rules.why: The insert pockets of a large part that was already printed were moved in the model and had to be rolled back. A whole concept was built on a wrong idea of what was printed.
fix_order: Read the print ledger for the part and its mates.
Keep the interface of a printed part; put the change into the unprinted mate.
The interface must move: say what happens to the printed copy and ask the owner.

attest.question: Is a copy of this part or of a part it mates with already printed, and did this change move, resize or remove an interface?
labels: no copy of this part or of a mate is printed (print ledger read)
a copy is printed; no interface moved, the printed copies still fit
a copy is printed and an interface moved: listed in the report for the owner with what happens to each printed copy

rules.title: Printed status is recorded data
rules.statement: The printed status of every part (printed or not, and which geometry was printed) is data in the print ledger. A plate name or a memory is not a record. A part with no record counts as printed.
rules.why: Printed status lived in plate names and in memory: nobody could say which geometry a printed part had.

rules.title: A printed part is still fixed in the model
rules.statement: A rule violation of a printed part is still fixed in the model, for the next print. No reprint is asked for. Unprinted mates stay compatible with both the printed copy and the fixed model. A bench instruction covers the printed copy.
rules.why: "Printed parts are frozen" and "what is printed is fixed in the model too" both stood. The pockets of a printed part were moved; its unprinted mate then got slots that fit both.
rules.note: Two accepted rules met here; this is one rule with the condition under which each holds.

rules.title: Every change says what happens to the printed copy
rules.statement: Every model change of a printed part states what happens to the printed copy: usable as it is, a hand patch, or a reprint.
rules.why: No lost print is on record. Without the line the owner learns at assembly that the part on the bench no longer matches the model.

rules.title: A flawed print is critical or tolerable, and the owner decides
rules.statement: A defect of a printed part is one of two classes, and the owner decides: critical (the model changes and the part is reprinted before assembly) or tolerable (patched by hand now, fixed in the model for the next print). Both actions are recorded. A tolerable part is never reprinted unasked.
rules.why: No lost print is on record. Without both entries the model fix of a hand-patched part is forgotten until the same flaw is printed again.
